questions.question: 'Milind Panho' is in the form of a dialogue between King Milind and Buddhist Saint. The concerned saint was -
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Nagasena__.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The Milindapanho is a Buddhist text from sometime between 100 BC and 200 AD.
 
• It purports to record a dialogue between the Indian Buddhist sage Nagasena, and the Indo-Greek king Menander of Bactria, who reigned in the 2nd century BC.
 
• The Milinda Panha is canonical in Burmese Buddhism, included as part of the book of Khuddaka Nikaya.
 
• An abridged version is included as part of Chinese Mahayana translations of the canon.
 
• The Milinda Panha is not regarded as canonical by Thai or Sri Lankan Buddhism, despite the surviving Theravada text being in Sinhalese script.
 
• The Chinese text titled the Monk Nagasena Sutra corresponds to the first three chapters of the Milindapanha.

questions.question: North-west part of the Indian peninsula was converted into a great centre of vulcanicity in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option** __1__**, i.e. **__the end of Cretaceous period.__**

**__The Cretaceous__**

**No **other geological system **shows a more widely divergent facies of deposits** in the different areas **of India** than the Cretaceous and there are few which cover such an extensive area of the country as this system does in its varied form.

 
• The **Southern Sea** at the same time **encroached on the Coromandel Coast**, and extended much further north, **overspreading Assam and probably flooding a part of the Indo-Gangetic depression**.
 
• It is noteworthy that **no communication existed between these two seas** - of Assam and the Narbada valley - although separated by only a small distance of intervening land.

While such was the geography of the rest of India, **towards the end of the Cretaceous the north-west part of the Peninsula was converted into a great centre of vulcanicity** of a type which has no parallel among the volcanic phenomena of the modern world.

questions.question:
Which one of the following is not correctly matched?

A. Article 153 - Office of the Governor

B. Article 154 - Executive Authority of the Governor

C. Article 155 - Removal of the Governor

D. Article 156 - Term of the Governor
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 153:** This article provides for the **Office of the Governor** in each state. It allows one person to be appointed as the governor of two or more states.
 
• **Article 154:** It vests the **Executive Authority of the State** in the Governor, who acts as the constitutional head of the state.
 
• **Article 155:** This article deals with the **Appointment of the Governor** by the President of India, not with the removal of the Governor.
 
• **Article 156:** It outlines the **Term of Office of the Governor**, which is normally five years, but the governor serves at the pleasure of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Removal of Governor:** There is no specific article for the removal of the governor. The governor holds office at the pleasure of the President, as implied in Article 156.
 
• **Governor's Role:** The governor acts as the constitutional head of the state, with powers related to the executive, legislative, and judicial functions.
 
• **Appointment (Article 155):** The governor is appointed by the President based on the advice of the central government.
 
• **Term (Article 156):** Though the tenure is fixed for five years, the governor can be removed earlier by the President or may resign voluntarily.
 
• **State Executive:** Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the structure, powers, and functions of the state executive, including the governor.

questions.question: Palaeontological evidences for evolution refer to the
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• The **theory of evolution** by **natural selection** was proposed by **Charles Darwin**.
 
• It stated that all life forms arise due to natural selection of small inheritable changes that increase the survivability of a species.
 
• Darwin also defined evolution as descent with modification, meaning we have evolved from our ancestors through inheritable variations of characteristics.
 
• **Palaeontological evidences** are one of the prime evidences for evolution of life-forms

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

**Paleontological Evidence** -

__
 
• It **refers to the fossils** that give us **indications of evolution** of organisms.
 
• Fossils are remains of organisms that existed thousands or millions of years ago.
 
• These fossils are **found in rocks** that form **different sedimentary layers** in the Earth's crust.
 
• A cross-section of these layers shows that different sedimentary layers contain fossils of different life-forms.
 
• The age of these layers also provides the **age of the fossils** and hence we can gather the period of time when those life-forms existed..
 
• Study of fossils have revealed that **different life forms existed in different geological time-periods** and **similarities exist between existing and pre-existing life forms**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Other Evidences** -

 
• **Anthropogenic Evidence** -

 
 
• Overuse of pesticides and herbicides have resulted in natural selection of resistant varieties in much lesser time.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Anatomy & Morphology** -
 
 
• Homology and analogy are based on comparisons between structure and functions of organs that show evolutionary adaptations in nature.
 
 
 
• **Embryological Evidence** -
 
 
• The presence of some features in embryonic stages of all vertebrates and their absence in adult stages suggest common ancestry.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor's court painters migrated to other provincial courts in Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

• Aurangzeb was the emperor of India from **1658 to 1707 AD**.
 
• The Mughal king **Aurangzeb's court painters** migrated a lot to provincial courts in **Rajasthan**.
 
• **Aurangzeb did not encourage painting** so a large number of the painter's started migrating.

questions.question: Ujjain served as the capital for which of the following rulers of Gupta dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ujjain served as the capital under the reign of **Chandragupta II**, also known as Chandragupta Vikramaditya, one of the most renowned rulers of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• The city of Ujjain was a significant cultural and political center during Chandragupta II's rule, known for its contributions to art, architecture, and literature.
 
• Chandragupta II expanded the Gupta Empire significantly and promoted trade, making Ujjain a hub for economic and cultural activities.
 
• Ujjain is historically associated with the legendary poet and playwright **Kalidasa**, whose works flourished during Chandragupta II's reign.
 
• The Gupta era under Chandragupta II is often referred to as the "Golden Age" of India due to advancements in science, mathematics, astronomy, religion, and philosophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta I**

 
 
• Chandragupta I was the founder of the Gupta Empire and ruled from around 319 CE.
 
• He is credited with laying the foundation of the Gupta dynasty and initiating the period of economic prosperity and cultural renaissance.
 
• He married Kumaradevi from the Lichchhavi dynasty, which strengthened his empire politically and territorially.
 
• Pataliputra served as the capital during his reign, not Ujjain.
 
 
 
• **Skandagupta**
 
 
• Skandagupta was a later ruler of the Gupta dynasty and is known for successfully defending the empire against invasions by the Huns.
 
• He took significant measures to restore the economy and administration after the Huna invasions.
 
• Though he was a strong ruler, there is no historical evidence suggesting Ujjain was his capital; he ruled primarily from Pataliputra.
 
 
 
• **Samudragupta**
 
 
• Samudragupta was a famous Gupta ruler known for his military conquests and patronage of art and culture.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" for his extensive campaigns across the subcontinent.
 
• Pataliputra remained the capital during his reign, and Ujjain did not serve as a capital under him.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right of Conquest - Sikkim**

 
 
• The British applied the right of conquest to annex territories they won through military campaigns. Sikkim was annexed by the British using this principle.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Lapse - Udaipur**
 
 
• Introduced by Lord Dalhousie, the Doctrine of Lapse allowed the British to annex any princely state where the ruler did not have a direct heir. Udaipur was one of the states affected by this policy.
 
 
 
• **"Good of the Governed" - Oudh**
 
 
• The British justified the annexation of Oudh by claiming it was for the "good of the governed," citing misrule by the local rulers. This paternalistic approach was a common pretext for British annexation.
 
 
 
• **Abolition of Regal titles - Tanjore**
 
 
• The British abolished the regal titles of local rulers to undermine their authority and integrate the regions directly into British India. Tanjore was one of the areas affected by this policy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Right of Conquest**

 
 
• British expansion in India often involved military conquest. Territories won in battle were annexed under the right of conquest.
 
 
 
• **Doctrine of Lapse**
 
 
• Lord Dalhousie's policy led to the annexation of several Indian states without direct male heirs, including Jhansi, Satara, and Nagpur, besides Udaipur.
 
 
 
• **"Good of the Governed"**
 
 
• This paternalistic justification was used to portray British rule as beneficial for the local population, often to mask imperial ambitions.
 
 
 
• **Abolition of Regal titles**
 
 
• The abolition of royal titles was part of the British strategy to erode the traditional authority of local rulers and integrate their territories into the British Empire.

questions.question:
Which of the following provisions can be amended by a special majority of Parliament without the consent of States?

1. Rules of procedure in Parliament

2. Fundamental Rights

3. Directive Principles of State Policy

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 and 3 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A number of provisions in the Constitution can be **amended by a simple majority of the two Houses of Parliament outside the scope of Article 368. **These provisions include:

 
 
• Quorum in Parliament
 
• Salaries and allowances of the members of Parliament
 
• **Rules of procedure in Parliament. *Hence, statement 1 is not correct.***
 
• Privileges of the Parliament, its members, and its committees
 
• Use of English language in Parliament
 
 
 
• The majority of the provisions in the Constitution need to be amended by a special majority of the Parliament, that is, a majority of the total membership of each House and a majority of two-thirds of the members of each House present and voting. The provisions which can be amended this way include:
 
 
• Fundamental Rights
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy
 
 
 
• *Hence, statement 2 and 3 are correct.*
 
• Those provisions of the Constitution which are related to the federal structure of the polity can be **amended by a special majority of the Parliament and also with the consent of half** **of the state legislatures by a simple majority. **The following provisions can be amended in this way:
 
 
• Election of the President and its manner.
 
• The extent of the executive power of the Union and the states.
 
• Supreme Court and high courts.
 
• Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the state.

questions.question: Which of the following vitamin require sunlight for its synthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vitamin D** is a fat-soluble vitamin that plays a crucial role in calcium absorption, bone health, and immune system regulation.
 
• It is synthesized in the human skin when exposed to sunlight, specifically ultraviolet B (UVB) rays.
 
• Sunlight exposure triggers the conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the skin to vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol), which is then activated by the liver and kidneys.
 
• Vitamin D deficiency can lead to conditions such as rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults, and an increased risk of osteoporosis.
 
• It is also obtained from dietary sources like fatty fish, fortified foods, and supplements, but sunlight remains the primary natural source for its synthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin B12**

 
 
• Vitamin B12, also known as cobalamin, is a water-soluble vitamin essential for red blood cell formation, neurological function, and DNA synthesis.
 
• It is primarily obtained from dietary sources like meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. It is not synthesized by the body or dependent on sunlight exposure.
 
• A deficiency in vitamin B12 can lead to anemia, fatigue, nerve damage, and cognitive impairments.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin C**
 
 
• Vitamin C, or ascorbic acid, is a water-soluble vitamin that acts as a powerful antioxidant, supports the immune system, and aids in collagen production.
 
• It is found in fruits and vegetables such as oranges, strawberries, bell peppers, and broccoli.
 
• Unlike vitamin D, vitamin C is not synthesized in the body and must be obtained through diet.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin A**
 
 
• Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin important for vision, immune function, and cell growth.
 
• It is obtained from animal-based foods as retinol (preformed vitamin A) and from plant-based sources as beta-carotene (a provitamin A carotenoid).
 
• Vitamin A does not require sunlight for its synthesis, as it is entirely dependent on dietary intake.

questions.question:
Consider the following:

**Assertion (A):** Harshavardhana convened the Prayag Assembly.

**Reason (R):** He wanted to popularise only the Mahayana form of Buddhism.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __***A is true, but R is false ***__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Harshavardhana convened the **Prayag Assembly in 643 AD**, but it was **not for the sole purpose of popularizing Mahayana Buddhism. **
 
• The Prayag Assembly was a grand assembly of all classes of people, regardless of their religion or social status. 
 
• It was also a religious assembly, but it was open to all religions, not just Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• The Prayag Assembly was a significant event in Harshavardhana's reign, as it demonstrated his commitment to religious tolerance and his desire to unite his kingdom. 
 
• It was also an opportunity for Harshavardhana to showcase his wealth and power, and to gain the support of his subjects.
 
• While **it is true that Harshavardhana was a devout Mahayana Buddhist,** he did not try to impose his religion on his subjects. 
 
• He was tolerant of all religions, and he supported the growth of all religious communities in his kingdom. 
 
• The Prayag Assembly is a reflection of Harshavardhana's commitment to religious tolerance and his vision for a united India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Health in the Indian Constitution:

Statement-I: The right to health is explicitly mentioned as a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution.

Statement-II: The Supreme Court has interpreted the right to life under Article 21 to include the right to health.

Which of the following is correct with respect to the above statements?

options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The right to health is not explicitly mentioned as a fundamental right in the Indian Constitution under Article 21.
 
• The Supreme Court has interpreted the right to life under Article 21 to include the right to health through various judgments.
 
• The right to health is derived from the interpretation of the right to life, emphasizing a dignified and quality life for all citizens.
 
• The judiciary has recognized access to healthcare and a clean environment as integral to the right to life under Article 21.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21:** Guarantees the fundamental right to life and personal liberty, interpreted broadly to include aspects of health, livelihood, and dignity.
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:** In cases like *Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India* and *State of Punjab v. Mohinder Singh Chawla*, the Supreme Court expanded the scope of Article 21 to include health-related rights.
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy:** Articles 38, 39(e), 41, and 47 emphasize the state’s role in ensuring public health, nutrition, and welfare.
 
• **Healthcare Schemes:** Programs like Ayushman Bharat aim to realize the vision of healthcare for all, aligning with the constitutional framework.
 
• **Right to Health:** While not explicitly mentioned as a fundamental right, it is enforceable indirectly through judicial activism and government policies.
 
• **Global Context:** The right to health is also recognized as a fundamental human right under international frameworks like the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) and the International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights (ICESCR).

questions.question: Which of the following vitamin deficiency causes Osteoporosis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vitamin D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vitamin D deficiency** is a leading cause of osteoporosis as it plays a critical role in calcium absorption and bone health.
 
• Without sufficient Vitamin D, calcium and phosphorus cannot be effectively absorbed, resulting in weakened bones and increased risk of fractures.
 
• Osteoporosis is a condition characterized by reduced bone density and increased fragility, often linked to prolonged Vitamin D deficiency.
 
• Vitamin D can be obtained through exposure to sunlight, dietary sources like fish, eggs, and fortified foods, or supplements.
 
• Regular screening for Vitamin D levels is recommended, especially for older adults, to mitigate the risk of osteoporosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Osteoporosis:** A condition where bones become brittle and weak, increasing susceptibility to fractures.
 
• **Calcium:** An essential mineral required for bone strength and density; its absorption is dependent on Vitamin D.
 
• **Vitamin K:** Plays a role in bone metabolism but is not directly linked to osteoporosis caused by Vitamin D deficiency.
 
• **Sources of Vitamin D:** Sunlight exposure, fatty fish (like salmon and mackerel), egg yolks, fortified milk, and supplements.
 
• **Risk Factors for Deficiency:** Limited sun exposure, aging, darker skin, and certain medical conditions like kidney disease can lead to Vitamin D deficiency.
